item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 101143
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center has issued its last advisory on
Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias, located inland over central Alabama.
Future advisories will be issued by the Weather Prediction Center
beginning at 10 am CDT.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Berg
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Summary for Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias (AT4/AL092026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FLASH FLOODING RISK CONTINUES WITH ISAIAS... As of 10:00 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 the center of Isaias was located near 32.8, -86.8 with movement NNW at 10 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1006 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 35 mph.

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias Public Advisory Number 16
item.description: The NHC has issued its final advisory on this system. Public Advisories from the Weather Prediction Center will provide updates as long as the system remains a flood threat. Issued at 1000 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 2026

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias Forecast Discussion Number 16
item.description:
Issued at 1000 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTNT44 KWNH 101459
TCDAT4
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias Discussion Number  16
NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD   AL092026
1000 AM CDT Sat Oct 10 2026

Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with post-tropical cyclone Isaias will 
continue across the Southern Appalachians and Southeast today. 
Considerable flash and urban flooding will be possible. Landslides 
are also possible across the Southern Appalachians.
 
2. Strong wind gusts continue to pose a threat across the 
southeastern United States today, including Georgia, the southern 
Appalachians, and extending west through much of central and 
northern Alabama, Mississippi, and Tennessee. Scattered power 
outages and downed trees and powerlines may occur, with the risk 
highest in elevated terrain.

3. Swells from Isaias will continue to affect much of the Gulf 
coasts of the United States, Mexico, and western Cuba this weekend. 
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather 
office.

4. A couple of tornadoes are possible today across eastern Georgia 
and the Carolinas.
